1: ls -l shows mode bits: rwx for user, group, other. chmod changes them.
chmod u+x file adds execute for the owner; chmod o-w removes write for others.
A directory needs the x bit to be entered (cd). r lets you list it.
2: chown user:group file changes ownership; sudo is required for files you don't own.
The setuid bit shows as an 's' in the user execute slot (ls -l). Remove with chmod u-s.
stat -c '%a %U:%G' FILE prints exactly what the grader looks at.
